item.statement: Buffer-bound safety. For every valid invocation, the candidate must perform no read outside the supplied source buffer region and no write outside the supplied H*P-element output buffer region, including when P > W.

plans.objective: Directly observe on the target that one valid candidate run issues no read outside the W*H source region and no write outside the H*P output buffer, using a P > W configuration.
plans.observation: Post-run target output buffer contents, the before/after guard canary slot values, and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report emitted during the run.
plans.pass_condition: Accept if (1) no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted; (2) the before and after guard canary slots equal their recorded baseline sentinel values; and (3) at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization, proving the kernel actually executed and wrote within the buffer. Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary.
plans.setup: On the target, build the unmodified candidate kernel. Place the W*H source region so that both the preceding and following pages are inaccessible (or run under the target memory-bounds checker that reports every out-of-region access). Use W=257, H=129, P=320 (P > W), shiftX=5, shiftY=7. Allocate the output buffer of exactly H*P elements, initialize every output slot and one guard canary slot immediately before and one immediately after the buffer to a distinct sentinel, and fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel. Record the baseline canaries, run one valid invocation, synchronize, and read back the buffer and canaries.

plans.objective: Prove from the future Ascend-C candidate kernel source that every source read and every output write the candidate can issue for a valid invocation lies inside the supplied source W*H logical region and the H*P output buffer, explicitly including configurations where P > W.
plans.observation: The submitted Ascend-C candidate source artifact's loop/tile bounds and its source-index and destination-index expressions, consumed by reading the candidate kernel file.
plans.pass_condition: Accept only when every reachable access is provably in bounds: the source offset is always in [0, W*H) for all valid x, y, shiftX, shiftY (for example floor_mod(x+shiftX, W) + W*floor_mod(y+shiftY, H), or an equivalent integer expression), and the destination offset is always in [0, H*P) (for example y*P + x with 0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H, or any other expression whose value is always within [0, H*P)). Reject if any reachable path can compute a negative source/destination offset, a source offset >= W*H, or a destination offset >= H*P, including when P > W.
plans.setup: Read the candidate artifact that implements the migrated shiftPitchLinear kernel. Locate the logical-coordinate loops or tiles and expand any vectorized/tiled access back to individual logical (x,y) elements. Record the exact source-index expression (or equivalent address arithmetic) and destination-index expression used by each access, including any guards or modulo operations.

plans.objective: Stress the buffer-bound property at small boundary shapes and boundary shifts, always with P > W, to catch one-past-the-end or negative-index accesses that only occur at edges.
plans.observation: For each boundary configuration, the post-run output guard-canary values and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report produced by that run.
plans.pass_condition: Accept only if, for every configuration, no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted, both output guard canaries equal their baseline sentinel values, and at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization (proving the kernel executed for that shape). Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary in any configuration.
plans.setup: On the target, build the unmodified candidate kernel and run a sweep over small shapes with padding, e.g., W in {1,2,3,16}, H in {1,2,3}, P = W + 3, and shiftX/shiftY in {0,1,W-1,W,W+1} plus -1 where representable, all satisfying the admitted domain. For each configuration, bracket the H*P output buffer with sentinel guard canaries, initialize every output slot to a distinct sentinel, fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel, and protect the pages around the W*H source region as in the runtime-observation plan. Run, synchronize, and record canaries and any fault/report for each configuration.
